sentences.text: Escherichia fergusonii is a member of the Enterobacterales that has only recently been recognised, and is reported together with Escherichia albertii as an emerging pathogen of humans and animals.
It has been isolated mainly from extraintestinal infections in humans and from various animal species.
A survey of faecal samples from farm animals throughout Japan reported it in 37.4% of swine, 46.2% of poultry and 17.1% of cattle samples.
Another study describes it as an emerging food-borne opportunistic pathogen and reports that, in mice, gut colonisation induced dysbiosis and worsened Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia.
A carbapenem-resistant clinical isolate carrying blaNDM-5 on an IncX3 plasmid was reported from a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province, China.
